solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Judge evicts Henry from more fashionable pad

indicators.note: to evict is to throw out, so one letter is removed from the following word
names the word the evicted letter is taken out of

parts.note: hotter means trendier, more in vogue
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A judge throws a man called Henry out of a trendier flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' looks like a home, picking up 'more fashionable', but it is a notepad.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad or small notebook for jotting things down is a pad.

clue.text: Amateur's gripped by enthusiasm for sound of tuba

indicators.note: being gripped means being held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: oomph is energy or zest
A is an abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: An amateur brass player is carried away by the tuba's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Oompah imitates the deep rhythmic blast a tuba or other bass brass instrument makes.

clue.text: To finish, call in on mischief maker

parts.note: to term something is to call or name it
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and folly

explanation.surface: Someone stops by on a troublemaker to bring matters to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate, Greek goddess of mischief and ruin, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to end or conclude something.

clue.text: Ringing one's mobile in foreign country? That's a non-starter

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the shortened country name
a non-starter loses its start, so the first letter of the country goes

parts.note: France is a country foreign to a British setter

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with the s, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Calling one's mobile phone while abroad turns out to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like a phone; it signals ONES rearranged to ESON, placed in RANCE (France minus its first letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is a ringing, reverberating quality in a sound.

clue.text: Son needs fix, getting stoned — that's said to impress

parts.note: to hang a picture is to fix it on a wall

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: stoned on drugs means high

explanation.surface: A son needing a drug fix gets stoned, apparently trying to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' here is the old sense of forcing someone into naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai a sailor was to force him into service, which is what press gangs did when they impressed men.

clue.text: Easy on the drink? Not at all

definitions.text: Easy on the drink? Not at all

parts.words: Easy on the drink? Not at all
parts.note: the drink is crossword slang for the sea, and someone far from easy at sea is queasy

explanation.surface: Someone is asked if they go easy on alcohol, and firmly denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' looks like alcohol but means the sea; being not at all easy afloat means feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea from a ship's motion is the condition of being uneasy on the ocean.

clue.text: A vehicle's stopped short on street! Stop!

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van has halted abruptly in the road and someone shouts for it to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical command meaning stop or cease.

clue.text: Maxim Gorky's capital — not so this writer

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial one, so the first letter of the name is taken

parts.note: no is a reply meaning not so
the setter referring to himself gives me

explanation.surface: Maxim Gorky, the Russian writer, and his city, compared with the crossword setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like Gorky's first name but is the definition, a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a short pithy saying or aphorism, as is a maxim.

clue.text: A couple of Scotsmen on special horses

parts.note: Rab and Ian are typical Scottish men's names
Ian is the second Scottish name

explanation.surface: Two Scots ride particular horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabians are a breed of horse prized for speed and stamina.

clue.text: American wild boar is lovely food

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: American wild boar is said to make a delicious meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like it describes the boar but signals BOARIS rearranged to BROSIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so it stands for anything delicious to eat.

clue.text: Alternative ways of portraying a night's coat

parts.note: night sounds like knight, and chess notation writes a knight as N, giving a plus N
or joins alternatives, the choice between two ways of writing the piece
older chess books wrote the knight as K, giving a plus K

explanation.surface: Different ways of depicting nightfall are offered.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'night' as the chess knight: written as N in modern notation and K in old notation, giving A N, OR, A K.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, a kind of outer garment.

clue.text: A bloomer, ignoring motor race

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: a carnation is a flower, something that blooms
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A blunder has been made, with no regard for a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a mistake, and 'motor race' seems one phrase; they split into a flower, a car and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A race can mean a people sharing descent or culture, a sense close to a nation.

clue.text: Prevailing but undecided when following up

definitions.meaning: something in the atmosphere or widely felt, like a mood that is current
placed after the word up the phrase means unsettled, not yet decided

explanation.surface: Something is widespread but still unresolved when chased up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' is not a link: prefix it to the answer to get the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling that is widely sensed is said to be about; put after up, the phrase means still unresolved.

clue.text: What about keeping uniform's colour?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece goes inside the other
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the colour of a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns EH into HE, which keeps U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a shade or tint, another word for a colour.

clue.text: An extremely awesome Ian Rankin novel I abandoned for another book

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
abandoned means left behind, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the letter I, taken as written

explanation.surface: Swapping a superb Ian Rankin crime novel for a different book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like Rankin's book but signals a rearrangement of AE (ends of awesome) and ANRANKIN (Ian Rankin minus I). Ian Rankin is a Scottish crime writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's novel is a book, and the clue mentions a novel already, hence another.

clue.text: Popular doctor's surgery succeeded after turning back a right shower?

indicators.note: after puts the reversed pair in front of the rest
turning back means reversing, so the two letters run the other way

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
an op is a surgical operation
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A well-liked GP's practice did well after a change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'shower' as a definition by example: a fall of drops, not a bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from clouds in drops is what a shower consists of.

clue.text: Nobody in yet? Not unusual around noon

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters go around the single letter
unusual signals the letters are shaken into an odd order

explanation.surface: Nobody has arrived yet, which is not unusual near midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nobody' looks like part of the surface sentence but it is the definition; INYETNOT is rearranged around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance is a nobody.

clue.text: Pop featuring in a recording gets European award

indicators.note: a thing featuring in another appears inside it

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording
cola is a fizzy drink, pop

explanation.surface: A pop song on a record wins a European prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests music but is a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an honour or token of praise, such as a prize.

clue.text: Speeding things up in case engineer's real busy

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lawsuit is an action, a legal case
CE stands for civil engineer

indicators.note: busy suggests bustle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer is genuinely busy hurrying things along, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' is not a phrase: case is a legal ACTION, holding CE plus LERA (REAL rearranged).
explanation.definitionFit: Acceleration is an increase in speed, the act of making things go faster.

clue.text: A stretch of grazeable area

indicators.note: a stretch is a run of the letters within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An expanse of land suitable for grazing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or pasture, open grassland where livestock feed.

clue.text: Bow is needed by the woman with yen for this?

definitions.text: Bow is needed by the woman with yen for this?

parts.note: a bow is a curve, an arc
her refers to a woman
Y is the symbol for the yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: A woman with a longing for a sport needs a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting with bow and arrow is the sport that a bow is needed for.

clue.text: Deny one's to appear in Dutch broadcast

indicators.note: appearing in something means being inside it

parts.note: seed broadcast by hand is sown
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to go on a Dutch TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests TV but means scattered like seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge or reject, a strong form of denial.

clue.text: Opinionated creature married a jerk

parts.note: a dog is a creature
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A bossy animal wed a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatic people assert their views as certain and will not accept disagreement.

clue.text: Mass exodus originally added to general confusion

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: A mass departure leads to widespread chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused struggle or jumble of people.

clue.text: Flag associated with English island

parts.note: to flag is to tire, to lose energy

explanation.surface: A flag linked with an English island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner but is the verb to weaken. Tiree is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiree is one of the Inner Hebrides, an island off western Scotland.

clue.text: Guy did trespass, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to trespass in the biblical sense is to sin

explanation.surface: A man broke the rules, as he admits when thinking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a man, and Dennis is a man's first name.

clue.text: Screw jack's given trouble? Let me see …

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
to ail is to trouble or afflict
er is the hesitant sound someone makes while thinking

explanation.surface: A man called Jack gets into difficulty and stalls while thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British slang for a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British prison slang a warder is called a screw.

clue.text: Proposal to include chapter on John Le Carré's central character, Smiley?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the next piece follows the single letter
the central character is the middle letter of the name
including something means holding it inside

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A plan to add a chapter about George Smiley, Le Carré's spy hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central character' suggests George Smiley but means the middle letter of JOHN LE CARRE. Smiley, the definition, is a smiling face symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face typed in a message is the best known kind of emoji-like symbol.

clue.text: Look at bank's investing very critically

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to see is to look at
to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: A financial look at a bank's investments, made with a very harsh eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' suggests money but means wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely means seriously or gravely, as in critically ill.

clue.text: Army's beaten, defending northern city of old

indicators.note: defending means guarding, so the letters surround the other piece
beaten means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: A defeated army guards an ancient northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: Smyrna was the ancient city that is now Izmir in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Smyrna was an ancient Greek city on the Aegean coast, now called Izmir.
